idiom_name: GObject screen-state object with properties and notify signals (GTK); plain struct plus callbacks without a toolkit
implementation_notes: The full structure is hand-written: a screen-state object (a GObject subclass when GTK/GObject is present) declares its dynamic fields as properties so the view can read and write them through the property API, and the view connects to the GObject::notify signal - whose detail argument is the property name in the standard case - to reload the widgets it owns. GObject supplies change notification and, in GTK, g_object_bind_property can push a model property onto a widget property, but nothing binds the other direction for you: the save half (widget signal to model setter) and the derived decision properties (composer_enabled) remain ordinary C functions. Without a toolkit the same shape degrades to a struct of state plus an array of function pointers, with no notification at all - the view is called explicitly after each mutation.
pitfalls: Handlers connected with g_signal_connect are not disconnected when their user data dies - the GObject documentation is explicit that only finalisation of the emitting object disconnects them - so a destroyed view keeps receiving notifications unless the code disconnects or uses g_signal_connect_object (which the same page calls unsafe in threaded programs).
A GObject property announces only changes made through the property API (g_object_set/set_property or an explicit notify): assigning the struct field directly leaves the view stale.
g_object_bind_property binds in one direction per call; two-way synchronization needs a second binding or an explicit write-back, and the write-back loops when both sides always write.
